references.text: The Levites receive the tithe from Israel as their inheritance for their service in the tabernacle, illustrating how the tithe of livestock was used.
Regulations concerning the tithe every third year, which was to be given to Levites, foreigners, fatherless children, and widows.
During King Hezekiah's reforms, the Israelites brought tithes of cattle and sheep in abundance, in accordance with the law in 3 Mosebok.
The prophet Ezekiel uses the image of passing under the shepherd's staff as a reference to mustering and selection, just as the tenth animal was chosen.
Jeremiah mentions the tithe in connection with God's covenant and blessings upon the people.
The immediately preceding verse deals with the tithe of the land's produce, which together with the tithe of livestock makes up the entire tithing system.
